## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Abhirūpanandātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.1) is a poem belonging to the *Therīgāthā* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It consists of verses 19 and 20 of the collection, which according to Dhammapāla's commentary (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*) were addressed by the Buddha directly to the nun Abhirūpanandā [Collett 2014]. In the commentarial account, Abhirūpanandā, excessively attached to and proud of her personal beauty, initially avoided an audience with the Buddha; upon finally appearing before him, the Buddha conjured a vision of a beautiful woman and made it wither away in front of her, inducing spiritual urgency (*saṃvega*) before uttering these verses on the impermanence and foul nature of the body [Collett 2014].

At the passage level, SuttaCentral records a curated parallel with the *Sundarīnandātherīgāthā* (Thig 5.4) [SuttaCentral], a text whose verses and commentarial backdrop closely parallel those of Abhirūpanandā [Collett 2014]. SuttaCentral also notes connections with the *Apadāna* biographies of Abhirūpanandā (*Abhirūpanandātherīapadāna*, Thi-Ap 36) and Khemā (*Khemātherīapadāna*, Thi-Ap 18) [SuttaCentral], whose poetic lines also interweave with this tradition [Collett 2014]. DharmaNexus identifies 27 Pali-internal text reuse matches across five texts, most extensively with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §0.3–2.4), the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā*, the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Khemātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 18), and the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus records an automatic cross-language match between segment §1.3 and two passages in the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (*Zá āhán jīng*, T 99, fascicle 45) [DharmaNexus]. English translations of the poem have been produced by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
